title: Getting Started with dv.spiderplot
text: creating spider plot module, need prepare clinical trial data. ’ll use example datasets pharmaverseadam package, provides CDISC ADaM-compliant datasets commonly used clinical trials.
code: adsl <- pharmaverseadam::adsl adtr <- pharmaverseadam::adtr_onco |>   dplyr::mutate(     ARM = factor(ARM, levels = c("Placebo", "Xanomeline Low Dose", "Xanomeline High Dose")),     SEX = factor(SEX, levels = c("F", "M"), labels = c("Female", "Male")),     AVISIT = forcats::fct_reorder(AVISIT, AVISITN)   )  # add back labels lost during data manipulation attr(adtr[["ARM"]], "label") <- "Planned Arm" attr(adtr[["SEX"]], "label") <- "Sex" attr(adtr[["AVISIT"]], "label") <- "Analysis Visit"  # add timestamp to be displayed in the app attr(adsl, "meta") <- list(mtime = Sys.time()) attr(adtr, "meta") <- list(mtime = Sys.time())

title: Getting Started with dv.spiderplot
text: Now data prepared, can configure spider plot module via mod_spiderplot() function. configuration defines spider plot behave options available users.
code: spiderplot_mod <- dv.spiderplot::mod_spiderplot(   module_id = "mod_spider",   subject_level_dataset_name = "adsl",   results_dataset_name = "adtr",   subjid_var = "USUBJID",   x_vars = c("ADY", "AVISIT"),   y_vars = c("PCHG", "CHG"),   color_vars = c("ARM", "AGEGR1"),   color_palette = c(     "Placebo" = "red",     "Xanomeline Low Dose" = "green",     "Xanomeline High Dose" = "blue"   ),   tooltip = c(     "Unique Subject Identifier: " = "USUBJID",     "Planned Arm: " = "ARM",     "Analysis Visit: " = "AVISIT",     "Days Since Randomization: " = "ADY",     "Change from Baseline: " = "CHG",     "Percent Change from Baseline: " = "PCHG"   ),   facet_rows = c("SEX", "ETHNIC"),   facet_cols = c("ARM", "AGEGR1"),   title = "Interactive Spider Plot",   subtitle = "CDISC-PILOT-01" )

title: Getting Started with dv.spiderplot
text: module configured, can now launch interactive spider plot application using DaVinci module manager.
code: dv.manager::run_app(   data = list("Demo" = list(adsl = adsl, adtr = adtr)),    module_list = list("Spider Plot" = spiderplot_mod),   title = "Spider Plot Demo",   filter_data = "adsl",   filter_key = "USUBJID",   filter_type = "datasets" )

title: Spider Plot Module — mod_spiderplot
text: module_id `[character(1)]`. Unique identifier module. subject_level_dataset_name `[character(1)]`. Name dataset containing subject level information (e.g., "adsl"). results_dataset_name `[character(1)]`. Name dataset containing analysis results (e.g., "adtr"). subjid_var `[character(1)]`. Variable name subject identifier. (e.g., "USUBJID"). x_vars `[character(1+)]`. character vector variable names x-axis. element must valid column name results dataset. Supported types numeric (e.g. "ADY") character/factor (e.g. "AVISIT"). multiple variables supplied (e.g., c("ADY", "AVISIT")), first element used default plot. y_vars `[character(1+)]`. character vector variable names y-axis. element must valid column name results dataset. Supported types numeric (e.g. "PCHG", "CHG"). least one valid variable required. color_vars `[character(1+) | NULL]`. Variable name(s) color grouping (e.g., treatment arm). color_palette `[named character(1+) | NULL]`. Custom color palette mapping factor levels (hex) colors. tooltip `[named character vector | NULL]`. Named character vector specifying tooltip content. Names labels, values column names. NULL, defaults using subject ID variable tooltips. facet_rows `[character(1+) | NULL]`. Variable names row faceting. (Splitting plot subplots rows) facet_cols `[character(1+) | NULL]`. Variable names column faceting. (Splitting plot subplots columns) height_default `[numeric(1) | NULL]`. Default plot height inches. NULL, defaults 5 inches. height_range `[numeric(2) | NULL]`. Range allowable plot heights inches. NULL, defaults c(1, height_default * 2). title `[character(1) | NULL]`. Main plot title. subtitle `[character(1) | NULL]`. Plot subtitle additional context. receiver_id `[character(1) | NULL]`. Module ID receive patient selection events module.

title: Build a collection of named constants — pack_of_constants
text: Shiny uses strings IDs link UI server elements. E.g:   foo_UI(id = ns("foo")) ...   foo_server(id = "foo") pattern makes easy programmers fall trap modifying one instance string literal "foo" without modifying rest unaware problem bug hit. also easy mistakes uses "foo" identifier uses (text labels, ...) , often case, parameter explicitly named. One easy fix consists using global variables instead plain string literals. case previous example, mean:   ID_FOO <- "foo"   foo_UI(ns(ID_FOO)) ...   foo_server(ID_FOO) simple addition makes purpose ID_FOO clear also fails gracefully ID_FOO instances updated synchronously along codebase. drawback polluting global namespace identifier variables. easily solved creating container constants, purpose pack_of_constants alias.  ID <- pack_of_constants(FOO = "foo", BAR = "bar")  ID$FOO  "foo"  ID$BA  Error `$.pack_of_constants`(ID, BA) :  Pack constants "ID" contain "BA" pack constants plain named list enforces elements unique, non-null names. tagged S3 object override extraction operators. use checkmate unnecessary, Good Library(TM) module rely anyways
